threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the ‘Overground’ instead of the ‘Ginger line’—bless your heart, you’ll learn soon enough.
Last night on the 77, a lad serenaded the whole bus with a harmonica. Weirdly, it made the 3 AM stop at Brixton feel like a gig.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler riding a tiny bike past the kebab stand, while an old man argued with a pigeon over a bread roll. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a busker playing saxophone at dawn by the canal, while joggers dodge their way past half-sleeping ducks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know the taco truck schedules better than bus times. It's an art form, really.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 Mission rolling past a street mural that has more layers than some city politics. Only in SF do art and transit collide like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every barra-cervesera is like in the guidebooks, but the real gems are the ones where the locals actually know your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their bewildered expressions when they realize how many different ways there are to order a coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver doesn’t say the stops; the locals just know to keep an eye out or check their phone.
Caught a guy on the 196 last night trying to sell his mixtape. He ended with a dramatic ‘next stop: fame!’ Classic Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really in Neukölln when I saw a spontaneous dance party break out in the subway station, complete with a saxophonist. Only here!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves vegan döner, complete with homemade sauces and a terrace that feels like an oasis.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can name the BART delays by heart, yet still shrug it off to grab a burrito at 11pm, while visitors panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 with a guy wearing a full tuxedo and flip-flops. Muni's a stage and we're all just characters in this wild play.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for lounging, but locals actually use them for gatherings and spontaneous parties. It's a whole vibe!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they refuse to learn the Catalan names on the metro maps—still staring at the screens like they're in a foreign country.
